scenes.text: Is our physical world just a shadow of true reality?
scenes.narration: Imagine looking at shadows on a wall and mistaking them for real objects. Plato argued that most of us live in this exact illusion every single day.

scenes.text: Checking score updates on your phone is not the same as watching the actual match.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday analogy to make this click. When you check cricket scores online, you only see data shadows, not the living match on the ground.

scenes.heading: Understanding Reality
scenes.narration: Heraclitus taught that everything in our world constantly changes, while Parmenides insisted that true reality never changes. Plato neatly combined both thinkers to shape his philosophy.

scenes.heading: Sophists Versus Socrates
scenes.narration: Unlike Sophists who charged money to teach selfish tricks, Socrates used dialectics, meaning logical debate. This guided conversation turns shallow beliefs into pure, virtue-giving knowledge.

scenes.heading: Plato's Myth of Metals
scenes.narration: Borrowing from Pythagoras, Plato divided human souls into three metals based on their dominant trait. Rulers must be men of gold guided by reason, rather than greed.

scenes.heading: Allegory of the Cave
scenes.narration: Plato used an allegory, a story with hidden meaning, about prisoners trapped inside a dark cave. They believe wall shadows are real until someone escapes outside to witness the sunlit truth.

scenes.name: Plato
scenes.idea: Reality is merely the shadow of permanent, unchanging ideas.
scenes.narration: Here is the big conclusion: physical things constantly decay, but their essence or idea remains permanent. Since only philosophers grasp these eternal ideas, Plato says they must rule.

items: Plato balanced Heraclitus' change and Parmenides' permanence.
Socratic dialectics turns basic belief into pure knowledge.
Ideas are permanent reality while physical things are shadows.
scenes.narration: To recap: Plato united change and permanence, trusted Socratic debate to reveal inner truth, and showed that ideas, not physical shadows, form ultimate reality.
